Package com.composum.platform.commons.util

Class CachedCalculation<T,​EXCEPTION extends Throwable>

  • java.lang.Object
    • com.composum.platform.commons.util.CachedCalculation<T,​EXCEPTION>
  • @ThreadSafe
public class CachedCalculation<T,​EXCEPTION extends Throwable>
extends Object
    Wrapper for an often needed expensive calculation that caches the result for a while and only repeats the calculation on when the value is requested and the cache timed out, and performs the neccesary locking to exclude parallel executions.

    • Constructor Detail

      • CachedCalculation

        public CachedCalculation​(@Nullable
                         @Nullable ExceptionThrowingSupplier<T,​EXCEPTION> supplier,
                         long timeoutMillis)
        Sets a timeout and a supplier for the value. The supplier can be set here, or given each time #giveValue(ExceptionThrowingSupplier), for instance if it needs resources which are not permanently available.
        Parameters:
        timeoutMillis - timeout in milliseconds
        supplier - a supplier; if this is null it has to be given in #giveValue(ExceptionThrowingSupplier).

      • giveValue

        @Nullable
public T giveValue​(@Nullable
                   @Nullable ExceptionThrowingSupplier<T,​EXCEPTION> currentSupplier,
                   boolean force)
            throws EXCEPTION extends Throwable
        Returns the cached value, calculating it if it wasn't calculated yet or timed out.
        Parameters:
        currentSupplier - the supplier with which this is to be calculated - for instance if there cannot be a permanently set supplier since it needs resources not always available. If null, the supplier given in the CachedCalculation(ExceptionThrowingSupplier, long) is used
        force - if true, the calculation is performed immediately, ignoring a cached value. This can be used if the calculation should be done in this thread. Using this instead of invalidate() means that the cached value can be used by other threads and enforces the calculation is done in this thread.
        Throws:
        EXCEPTION extends Throwable

      • invalidate

        public void invalidate()
        Invalidates the current value, enforcing a new calculation. Use when it is known that the value is wrong. If requests during the new calculation should still get the cached value, consider giveValue(ExceptionThrowingSupplier, boolean) with force=true.
